newsitem.title: UK: London gold slumbers, platinum probes $390 level.
newsitem.headline: London gold slumbers, platinum probes $390 level.

text.p: The gold market remained soporific on Wednesday, with trading limited to a tight price range with scant market activity.
Bullion fixed at $383.00 an ounce, compared to $382.90 in the morning and a Tuesday London close of $383.30/$383.80.
"There's not a lot to say. Gold's been on one side of $383 all day and it's moved in a tiny range," a dealer said. Bids were quoted so far between $383.10 and $382.40.
But several dealers said they were anticipating a limited shortcovering rally following the outcome of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) meeting to discuss proposed gold sales.
"The funds are short, thinking the IMF sale is a done deal, even though it looks like it may go the other way," a dealer said. "I wouldn't be surprised to see a shortcovering rally."
International monetary sources said earlier this week the IMF was running into problems agreeing the proposal to sell some five million ounces of gold to finance aid to poor nations.
Gold's $385 resistance level, where producer selling is expected to emerge, would most likely cap an rise, dealers said.
Support, however, was looking relatively healthy around $382. It was boosted by a recent increase in physical uptake out of Asia, notably Hong Kong and Singapore, dealers said.
Gold was little bothered by news that the U.S. trade deficit has surged to its highest level in more than eight years.
The market also ignored Gold Fields Mineral Services Gold 1996 report, which noted that a good Indian monsoon season boded well for gold demand in coming months.

Technical indicators were mixed for gold, said independent analyst Brian Marber. A possibility existed of moving up to around $384 in the short term, but the one-month moving average was close to bearishly crossing beneath the three-month.
A "black engulfer" pattern on the charts was an even more ominous sign, Marber said in a commentary.

Platinum showed sudden verve in the otherwise moribund complex by rallying and testing the $390 resistance level shortly before the gold fix. Dealers said brighter technicals were attracting trade and fund buying.
"It's looking quite positive on the charts, and if it closes on the highs it will look good for tomorrow," a dealer said.
Platinum was indicated at $390.00/$391.00, up $2 from Tuesday's London close. Its high bid so far was $390.80.
Silver was unchanged at $5.06/$5.08, while palladium was $0.50 easier at $120.75/$121.75.
